theme: 3 terms for SwiftUI animation: appearing, following a value and starting it yourself

terms.definition: The animation that a view uses when it appears or disappears.
terms.example: Add a Transition, so the banner slides in.

terms.definition: An animation that a view runs by itself whenever a watched value changes.
terms.example: Use an Implicit Animation, so the circle grows smoothly.
terms.code:
var big = false
Circle()
    .scaleEffect(big ? 2 : 1)
    .animation(.easeInOut, value: big)

terms.definition: An animation that you start yourself for one specific change.
terms.example: Use an Explicit Animation when the user taps the button.

video.title: Transition, Implicit Animation & Explicit Animation | Day 146
video.description:
Learn to explain how to animate a SwiftUI view: Transition, Implicit Animation & Explicit Animation, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Transition - The animation that a view uses when it appears or disappears.
Implicit Animation - An animation that a view runs by itself whenever a watched value changes.
Explicit Animation - An animation that you start yourself for one specific change.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.title: SwiftUI Transition, Implicit Animation & Explicit Animation | Day 146
landscape.description:
Explain Transition, Implicit Animation & Explicit Animation in SwiftUI by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
트랜지션, 암시적 애니메이션, 명시적 애니메이션 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Transition - The animation that a view uses when it appears or disappears.
한국어: 트랜지션: 뷰가 나타나거나 사라질 때 쓰는 애니메이션

Implicit Animation - An animation that a view runs by itself whenever a watched value changes.
한국어: 암시적 애니메이션: 지켜보는 값이 바뀔 때마다 뷰가 스스로 실행하는 애니메이션

Explicit Animation - An animation that you start yourself for one specific change.
한국어: 명시적 애니메이션: 특정한 변경 하나에 대해 직접 시작하는 애니메이션

landscape.hook: Can you explain Transition, Implicit Animation and Explicit Animation in English?

dialogue.title: A smooth circle

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, the circle jumps to the new size. I want it smooth.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Add an Implicit Animation. Use `.animation` with the value it should watch.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The Implicit Animation runs only when that value changes. Without it, too many things animate.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: OK. Now the Big text appears with no effect.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use a Transition. It decides how a view appears and disappears.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A Transition needs an animation, and the view must be added or removed with `if`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can I start the animation from the button instead?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, that is an Explicit Animation. Wrap the change in `withAnimation`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: An Implicit Animation follows a value. An Explicit Animation follows one change that you choose.
